definition: The stable that was home to all-time-great yokozuna Hakuho throughout his career; now operated by Hakuho himself.
Stable that produced two recent yokozuna: Harumafuji and the current Terunofuji.
Stable run by retired yokozuna Kisenosato; based in Matsudo, Chiba, it trains several active makuuchi wrestlers.
Stable later run by the legendary Chiyonofuji; continues to produce wrestlers bearing the 'Chiyono' prefix in their ring names.
One of the oldest continuously operating stables in professional sumo, tracing its lineage back many generations.
Run by former ozeki Kotooshu, a Bulgarian-born wrestler and the first European to reach sumo's second-highest rank.
Consistently fields the highest number of wrestlers in the makuuchi division of any single stable.
Historic stable that lends its name to one of the six main ichimon groupings that organise professional sumo.
Active stable run by former ozeki Goeido, one of the more decorated recent Japanese-born wrestlers.
Stable whose current stablemaster serves as chairman of the Japan Sumo Association.
Long-established stable based in Kōtō, Tokyo, with a history of producing consistent upper-division wrestlers.
Active Tokyo stable known for its international roster that has included wrestlers from Europe and Central Asia.
Stable run by former yokozuna Kakuryu after his retirement in 2021.
Prestigious stable that gives its name to the Nishonoseki ichimon, one of sumo's main governing factions.
Active stable based in Sumida, Tokyo, known for producing solid mid-division wrestlers over several decades.
